strongest_angle: Dental isotope analysis of tooth enamel combined with ancient DNA from human remains in Rupert's Valley on St Helena allows researchers to map the precise childhood origins of liberated Africans.

key_facts.fact: Researchers analyzed 193 tooth enamel strontium isotope measurements from 152 liberated Africans buried on St Helena to reconstruct their early-life geographic origins.
Historical records show that nearly 27,000 liberated Africans were brought to St Helena in the mid-19th century after Royal Navy ships intercepted illegal slave vessels.
The interdisciplinary study was led by researchers at the Globe Institute at the University of Copenhagen and UC Santa Cruz.
The transatlantic slave trade forcibly displaced more than 12.5 million Africans, making recovery of specific life histories a major priority for descendant communities.

quotes.text: Because enamel forms during childhood and adolescence and incorporates local dietary strontium, it preserves a geochemical record of early-life residence.
quotes.speaker: Xueye Wang et al.
